title: Is the trait turnover in the kind-specific-waste fed vortices real at dt/2 and on a 1.5x grid, does it act through local rarity, and does a labkit pack of that world keep I and D?
summary: The continuous-trait fed vortices with a kind-specific waste (20261027T1245-c58-vortex-waste-novelty, 1 component; 20261027T1401-c58-vortex-trait3d, 3 components) keep new trait classes taking over against a kind-blind twin, but no numerical check, no pack and no mechanism exist yet: births and fusions show no advantage for globally rare classes. One loop: (1) labkit packs of the 1-component world (ew 0.25, sw 0.4, mut_dt 50) on seeds 5 6 to T=6000 (--frames 2000 --spf 150), checking persistent splits and generation; (2) trait.py at world dt 0.01 and on a 192^2 grid with L, nu, kY, Dl, Dw, mut_r and the 2-px mask dilation rescaled by 1.5 (seed 1, T=6000), comparing first-time dominants after t=3000 and classes ever held by >= 3 with 20261027T1245's seed 1; (3) a local-rarity measure: for each split, fusion and fade, the share of the vortex's class among vortices within 22 px (the waste's reach), against the same for random vortices.
experiment: packs on seeds 5 6 (1-component waste world), trait.py at world dt/2 and 1.5x grid on seed 1, and a local-rarity version of freqbirth.py/fusion.py (needs vortex positions in traits_by_frame); about 60 cpu-minutes per run, 4 runs
